content.text:
**As of Wednesday 11 November 2026, both free tiers are $0 with no credit card. Neon's free tier is more generous on projects and database storage. Supabase's includes more bundled services such as auth, file storage and edge functions.**

## Neon Free
Neon's own docs and FAQ, published within the last week, give these limits:
-

content.text: It includes 100 projects, 10 branches per project, and 100 CU-hours of compute per project per month.

citations.cited_text: The Neon Free plan costs $0/month and includes 100 projects, 10 branches per project, 100 CU-hours of compute per project per month, 1 GB of Postgres ...
citations.title: What are the limits and quotas for Neon's Free plan? - Neon FAQs

content.text: Storage is 1 GB of Postgres per project, up to 20 GB across all projects.

citations.cited_text: The Neon Free plan costs $0/month and includes 100 projects, 10 branches per project, 100 CU-hours of compute per project per month, 1 GB of Postgres ...
citations.title: What are the limits and quotas for Neon's Free plan? - Neon FAQs

content.text: Public network transfer is 5 GB per project per month.

citations.cited_text: Computes scale to zero after 5 minutes of inactivity and can scale up to 2 CU (≈8 GB RAM) when active.
citations.title: What are the limits and quotas for Neon's Free plan? - Neon FAQs

content.text: Computes scale to zero after 5 minutes of inactivity and can scale up to 2 CU (about 8 GB RAM) when active.

citations.cited_text: Neon’s Managed Better Auth is included on every plan: up to 60,000 monthly active users per project on Free, and up to 1 million on Launch and Scale, ...
citations.title: Neon Pricing: The Honest Cost of Serverless Postgres

content.text: Neon's managed auth is included, with up to 60,000 monthly active users per project on Free.

This comes from a third-party source.

Some third-party pages still list 0.5 GB per project, or fewer projects. Neon's own pages say 1 GB, so I'd go with that. The older figures look outdated.

## Main differences
- **Idle behaviour:**

citations.cited_text: Supabase pauses Free Plan projects after a period of inactivity and requires a manual unpause, while Neon's scale-to-zero resumes automatically on eve...
citations.title: What are the best free or low-cost managed Postgres services for side projects that scale automatically when traffic picks up? - Neon FAQs

content.text: Supabase pauses Free projects after inactivity and needs a manual unpause, while Neon's scale-to-zero resumes automatically on each query.

That comparison comes from Neon's own FAQ, so it is not neutral.
- **Scope:** Neon is Postgres only, with branching. Supabase bundles auth, storage, realtime and edge functions around its database.
